messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@legacybank.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: on-prem air-gapped call — hardware & offline ops next steps

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great to walk through LegacyBank's on-prem requirements. Per our conversation, I wanted to document the items we discussed and the immediate next steps so all parties have the same view.

Recap (what you told us):
- Target environment: fully air-gapped branch data center for customer-facing NLP services (no egress to internet).
- Initial footprint: two inference clusters (prod + DR), each planned for ~150 QPS at median prompt sizes; spike to 400 QPS expected during batch windows.
- Hardware preference: you asked about supported GPU families and whether we can run on mixed-node racks (A100 + H100).
- Offline ops constraints: maintenance windows limited to 2 hours monthly; no outbound package downloads allowed.

Attachments: I attached our onprem_hardware_requirements_v2.pdf and the high-level architecture PNG. The PDF includes supported OS/hypervisor, driver stack, and preferred PCIe layouts.

Open questions / clarifications we need to move to an ops scoping call:
1) Can your infra team provide dedicated KVM/console access during initial install, or will everything be performed on-site with RackSolutions?
2) Confirm whether the racks will have NVLink fabric between GPUs or if nodes will be isolated (this affects preferred quantization/batching recommendations).
3) Do you have a preferred air-gap distro for package transfer (offline repo method) or do you want Redwood to prepare offline bundles?

Next steps (owners & timing):
- LegacyBank: share the full rack BOM and network diagram (Priya) — expected EOD Tue 4/16.
- Redwood SEs: ops scoping call to review install/runbook and offline bundle approach (Marissa to schedule with Dev/ Rishi).
- Rack partner: coordinate on console access and on-site install window (Alan Wu cc'd).

Can you confirm the BOM delivery timeline and preferred times for a 60‑minute ops scoping call next week?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa —

Quick answers while I gather the BOM:
- We'll have NVLink only on the H100 nodes; A100 nodes will be standalone. Expect mixed racks.
- RackSolutions will handle physical install; they can provide KVM access for initial setup if we white-list their engineers.
- We currently use an internal offline repo process (tarball + signed metadata). If Redwood can provide an encrypted offline bundle compatible with our verification process, that would be ideal.

I'll push the rack BOM and network diagram to Priya and aim to get it to you by EOD Monday 4/16.

Also: maintenance windows are tight — we can do a one-time 4-hour staging window during the first week of May for initial image installation, followed by a recurring 2-hour monthly window.

Marissa / team —

Thanks — quick technical replies inline and a suggested agenda for the ops scoping call.

Inline answers:
- Mixed racks (A100 standalone + H100 NVLink): we recommend placing shard-heavy, high-throughput models on H100 NVLink clusters to take advantage of inter-GPU communications for larger sequence lengths. A100 nodes are great for smaller models / lower latency per-token workloads. We'll include a proposed shard/instance mapping in the call.
- KV cache & batching: for mixed racks, we'll tune batching to prefer local GPU batching and fall back to cross-node batching only during batch windows. This keeps tail latency predictable.
- Offline bundle: Redwood can prepare an encrypted tarball signed with our private key; we can also provide a SHA256 checksum and PGP-signed manifest to fit your verification workflow. We'll need the public key or verification procedure from your security team.
- Staging window staffing: agree — recommend 2 SEs on the install call and 1 engineer for smoke tests post-install (we can be on-call for 48 hours to triage).

Proposed ops scoping call agenda (60 min):
1) Quick roll call & objectives (5m)
2) Rack BOM & network constraints review (10m)
3) Installer / offline bundle flow & verification (15m)
4) Staging plan & runbook walkthrough (15m)
5) Open Qs, timelines, and next steps (15m)

Availability: Dev (Tue 4/17 9-11am PT, Wed 4/18 8-12pm PT). Rishi can cover Wed morning.

I'll assemble a 1-page ops checklist for RackSolutions (hardware prechecks, console/KVM, IP assignments, firewall rules for intra-rack mgmt) and share before the call.

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
